::: {.callout-note}
## Status

This page introduces a tier conformance model proposed in
[ADR-076](../adr/adr-076-tier-conformance-model.qmd). The ADR is
currently **PROPOSED** — feedback welcome before ratification.
:::

Federal IT does not adopt software at one level. NIST CSF defines
four Tiers; CMMC defines three Levels; FedRAMP defines Low / Moderate /
High. Agencies are used to declaring **which level** of a capability
they have adopted, and recognizing that lower-level adopters consume a
strict subset of higher-level capabilities.

UIAO works the same way. An agency does not "adopt UIAO" — an agency
declares a tier per capability, picks the level of investment that
matches its program, and upgrades when ready. Lower-tier adoption
never breaks because of higher-tier work; higher-tier adoption never
forces lower-tier adopters to keep up.

## The Five Tiers

| Tier | Name | What it does | Where it runs | Examples |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Passive Observation | Reads agency systems. Reports. Never mutates. | Anywhere with read credentials. | Discovery scanners; drift detectors; validators; query CLI (`uiao query orgpath user@agency.gov`); OSCAL evidence emit. |
| **2** | Transformative Authoring | Reads agency systems; emits files (translations, plans, generated docs). Never mutates live systems. | CI, operator workstation. | Schema and document generators; AD-OU-to-OrgPath translators; GPO-to-Intune translators; migration plan generators. |
| **3** | Active Substrate | Mutates agency tenant state under controlled service account, with audit. | Agency-hosted service account. | Dynamic group writers; OrgPath value stampers; Conditional Access policy publishers; in-bounds drift remediators. |
| **4** | Active Services | UIAO-supplied services agencies deploy and run. These services own their own state. | Agency-deployed server (the Platform Server). | Platform Server (Windows Server 2025 + Gitea + IIS + OrgTree); KYC broker; operator web console; orchestrator daemon; evidence-fabric signing service. |
| **5** | Embedded Libraries | Code shipped to consumers — adapters, agency applications, third-party tooling. | Inside customer code. | PowerShell module; adapter SDK; policy-as-code DSL; validation libraries on PyPI / NuGet. |

A higher tier always includes the lower tiers as a strict subset.
An agency at Tier 4 for Identity is also implicitly conformant at
Tiers 1, 2, and 3 for Identity.

## The Five Capabilities

A capability is a coherent UIAO surface against which conformance is
declared independently. The initial set is fixed at five:

| Capability | Scope |
|---|---|
| **Identity** | OrgTree, OrgPath, dynamic groups, delegation, identity-related drift. |
| **Compliance** | SCuBA, FedRAMP, CISA, OSCAL evidence, control mapping, continuous monitoring. |
| **KYC** | Citizen↔agency and inter-agency identity verification, SSN-equivalent SSOT brokering. |
| **Substrate** | Operational tooling, PowerShell module, CLI, Quarto pipeline, generators. |
| **Platform** | Platform Server, deployed UIAO services, release artifacts, HA topology. |

Capabilities are added or revised only through ADRs. Five is the
floor; growth is bounded by ADR discipline.

## How to declare conformance

A conformance declaration is structured per capability, plus an
optional headline tier for procurement use:

```yaml
agency: Example Federal Agency
declared: 2026-05-22
conformance:
  Identity: 3      # Active Substrate — UIAO writes Entra
  Compliance: 2    # Transformative — UIAO generates OSCAL evidence locally
  KYC: 0           # Not declared
  Substrate: 2    # Transformative — agency runs UIAO CLI in CI
  Platform: 0     # Not declared — no Platform Server deployed
headline_tier: 3
headline_basis: Identity
```

Tier `0` means **not declared / not adopted**. It is not a level of
conformance; it is the absence of one.

A headline tier MUST cite the capability that justifies it. "Headline
Tier 4" without a per-capability breakdown is not a valid
declaration. Procurement decks may use the headline; auditors get
the full matrix.

## The backward-compatibility promise

Upgrading from Tier N to Tier N+1 in any capability MUST NOT require:

- re-stamping existing OrgPath values
- re-running migrations on already-migrated objects
- rewriting dynamic group rules authored at the lower tier
- modifying schemas of artifacts generated at the lower tier

Tier N+1 schemas, frontmatter fields, and artifact contracts are a
**strict superset** of Tier N. A change that breaks this rule
requires a new major Platform Server version and explicit migration
tooling shipped with it.

This is the discipline that makes incremental adoption possible.
Without it, "start at Tier 1" is a trap.

## GitHub vs the Platform Server

UIAO has two surfaces with distinct authority:

| Surface | Role | What it tells you |
|---|---|---|
| **GitHub repository** (this site) | Source. Pre-release. Architecture and tooling under active development. | What UIAO **is becoming**. Canon documents legitimately carry "Aspirational" labels — the repository is by definition pre-release. |
| **Platform Server** | Released, signed, revision-controlled artifact agencies deploy. | What UIAO **IS, at version X.Y.Z**. Customer guides describing v1.0 behavior describe deployed Platform Server behavior. |

A canon doc marked "Aspirational" and a customer guide marked
"v1.0 shipped" on the same subject are not contradictions — they are
correct claims about different lifecycle stages of the same code.

The release engineering layer that produces signed Platform Server
artifacts from the repository (tagged releases, SLSA provenance,
release channel, release notes with schema-compatibility
declarations, rollback path) is itself Tier 4 work and is in
development.

## Why this model

Five concrete conflicts in the published site motivated this model:

1. Canon labels things "Aspirational" while customer guides ship
   them as "v1.0." Resolved by the source / release distinction.
2. Different documents claim different counts of governance
   principles (7 / 3 / 1). Resolved by mapping principles to tiers —
   some universal, some applying only at higher tiers.
3. "Intune-First" means net-new procurement discipline in canon and
   GPO replacement in customer docs. Resolved by tier: Tier 1
   procurement discipline; Tier 3 active SLA validator; Tier 4
   Platform Server enforcement.
4. Directory Migration phase counts differ (5 / 10 / 6). Resolved
   as level-of-detail: canon's 5-phase view is the Tier-2
   plan-generator output; the longer customer phase lists are
   Tier-3 runbooks refining specific phases.
5. OrgPath attribute semantics differ (composite path vs single
   facet per slot). Resolved by tier: composite-path is a Tier 1
   expression of intent; single-facet-per-attribute is the Tier 3
   storage contract.

See [ADR-076](../adr/adr-076-tier-conformance-model.qmd) for the
full rationale, consequences, risks, and review triggers.
